benefit.name: Community Living BC (CLBC) Adult Supports
benefit.amount: Individually planned funded services — residential, employment, community inclusion, respite
benefit.summary: A provincial agency that funds lifelong supports for adults 19+ with developmental disabilities. Supports include home sharing and staffed living, employment services, community inclusion, respite and family support. Youth can apply from age 16. What funded support you get, and when, depends on how urgent your situation is and the funding CLBC has at the time of the request.

items: You are an adult 19 or older with significantly impaired intellectual and adaptive functioning that began before age 18.
Under the PSI stream, you are an adult with an FASD or autism spectrum diagnosis plus significant adaptive-functioning limitations.
eligibility.note: You can apply from age 16, and supports continue beyond 65.

benefit.requiresNote: Adults 19+ with significantly impaired intellectual and adaptive functioning that began before age 18; or, under the PSI stream, adults with an FASD or autism spectrum diagnosis plus significant adaptive-functioning limitations. Apply from age 16; supports continue beyond 65
benefit.note: There are two eligibility streams. Developmental Disability needs a psychologist's cognitive and adaptive assessments. The Personalized Supports Initiative needs an FASD or ASD diagnosis plus significant daily-living limitations. You do not need an intellectual disability for this stream. These assessments are sometimes already done when you were in school, so ask before arranging new ones.

detail.about: Services are delivered through a network of contracted agencies and planned individually with a CLBC facilitator.

items: Residential supports (living in your own place, shared living/home sharing with a contracted family, or staffed homes)
Employment support to find and keep a job
The Provincial Assessment Centre's mental-health services for people 14+ with developmental disabilities

steps: From age 16, ask your MCFD/CYSN worker about transition planning to CLBC
Contact your nearest CLBC office (1-877-660-2522) — a facilitator explains the required documents and approved assessors
Submit assessments and forms completed by an approved professional (registered psychologist for the DD stream); school-years assessments may be reusable
Once eligibility is confirmed, attend the CLBC Welcome Workshop series and work with your facilitator on a support plan
CLBC connects you to funded services based on the plan and available resources
documents: Cognitive/psychoeducational assessment by a registered psychologist (DD stream)
Adaptive functioning assessment completed by an approved professional
Confirmed FASD or autism spectrum diagnosis for the PSI stream
CLBC eligibility forms completed by approved professionals
tips: Start at 16, because assessments and planning take time. What funded support you get, and when, depends on how urgent your situation is and the funding CLBC has at the time of your request.
If you were assessed in school, ask the school district for copies. You may not need a new assessment.
Not eligible under the DD stream? Ask specifically about the Personalized Supports Initiative (PSI)
Respite or equivalent funding is commonly the first service offered to families of transitioning youth. Ask your facilitator what is available in your region.
Adults on CLBC services usually also qualify for BC PWD disability assistance. Apply for both.
detail.time: When funded support starts depends on how urgent your situation is and the amount of funding CLBC has at the time of the request.

meta.effort: Eligibility request + diagnostic and adaptive-function records
meta.wait: Not published — ask your local CLBC office
